referee_caveats_inferred: Nautilus density (4.6e4 cm-3) differs from the RADEX density (4.6e6 cm-3) with no justification of the mismatch.
A single-temperature (15 K) dust assumption and a fixed kappa give the mass and N(H2); no uncertainties are given for masses or abundances.
Several column densities rest on a single line with an assumed 2 arcsec source size; RADEX results are strongly degenerate.
Text and abstract quote slightly different temperatures (25 K vs 27 +/- 5 K for CH3CHO; 450 vs 460 K for 13CH3CN) and velocity values in the text differ from the line table.
The 450 K 13CH3CN result rests on marginal k-ladder detections (many lines at or below 0.15 K with ~5 sigma) and the Eu of 896.78 K for one CH3CH2CN line looks like a typo.
Hot (450 K) gas interpreted as protostar without continuum or line evidence of a protostar beyond temperature; no outflow tracer analysed in this paper.
The 'tail' being a separate source or part of the core is not resolved.
